overall.decision: Do not reuse old candidate_hygiene unchanged.
overall.assessment: Of15 flagged rows,11 are ordinary narrative content and1 is an ambiguous attraction-exhibited short. Only3 clearly support nonstandard-artifact identity; a further clear attraction is missed. This audit finds a high false-positive rate in the sampled flagged set, not a universal precision estimate.
overall.ordinary_scope: These are catalog hygiene candidates, not title quality judgments. Even clear attraction works may be relevant when the request explicitly seeks them.

proposed_conditions: Exclude from ordinary film/series search only when prose identifies the current record itself as an attraction/simulator experience, corroborated by audience seating/movement, ride installation, immersive display or explicit designed-as-attraction wording. A brand/venue mention alone is insufficient.

Never use a substring inside based on theme park ride, adaptation, setting, characters visiting a ride, or metaphorical thrill ride as identity evidence. Tags alone cannot establish current-record identity.

For pilots require current-record identification as an original/standalone pilot version AND explicit nonrelease/rejection, with no evidence that this same record became a released series or feature. Historical precursor-pilot mentions do not qualify.
Keep ambiguous shorts/films shown at parks. Missing distribution information is unknown, not exclusion evidence.
Rules must remain title-ID-free and query-independent except any explicit product/request media-scope choice; preserve matched source spans and rejection reasons. No paid planner gates.

cases.title: The Problem Solverz
cases.assessment: A rejected pilot is mentioned as development history; synopsis explicitly identifies the current released animated series and network premiere. Never exclude released series merely because a precursor pilot was rejected.
cases.source_excerpt:
The Problem Solverz is an American animated television series created by Ben Jones, a member of the art collective Paper Rad, for Cartoon Network. The series centered on the titular Problem Solverz trio of Alfe, Roba, and Horace, as they solve and sometimes create the various problems that plague their town, Farboro. The series is rated TV-PG. The original pilot Neon Knome was rejected by Cartoon Network's late-night programming block Adult Swim, but was picked up and re-tooled by the main network, which premiered the series on April 4, 2011.

On September 20, 2012, a statement on a Facebook page for the show said that the second half of Season 2 was intended to debut September 24, 2012, but the scheduling was delayed. Selected reruns have been aired during Cartoon Network's January 2013 revival of their Cartoon Planet variety show.
